**Owning seat claimed** — `domain:services` execution seat, PM session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`. Assigned to me as the decomposing seat, **not** as an implementer.

⛔ **This card is not dispatchable as a unit and I am not dispatching it.** Its own Discipline section says so: *"Contract-first decomposition by the owning seat: parent (this card) + sub-issues per surface, spec first, `Blocked-by:` chains between legs."* `has_children` is currently **false**, so that decomposition has not happened yet. Recording the shape now, before sub-issues are written, so the legs are not cut along the wrong seams.

## Three things that must be settled BEFORE the sub-issues can be scoped

**1. `sys_scim_provider`'s disposition is a DECISION, not a leg.** Scope item 1 says it is *"decided INSIDE this epic"* with the managed-catalog fact on the table — retire vs facade vs managed-catalog adoption. Several other legs' scope depends on which way it goes (the Setup surface's backend seam in particular). ⇒ It gets a **decision card of its own, ruled first**, not a task card someone starts and discovers is a fork. ⛔ Not mine to rule.

**2. The `packages/spec` leg is not this seat's.** Scope item 3 says it explicitly: *"`packages/spec` work goes to the spec seat per single-owner rule."* This lane has **zero ownership** there. That leg becomes a card in the spec lane with a `Blocked-by:` pointing at it from the legs that consume the parity result — the same contract-first shape as #10413 → #10576 and #10025 → #11504.

**3. Leg 4 has a prerequisite that is not ours to assume.** The parity-gate restructure depends on **#11380 / PR #11429**'s constructor fix — *"land or absorb it."* Whether it lands independently or gets absorbed changes whether leg 4 is one card or two. That needs checking against #11429's current state before the leg is written, not after.

## ⚠️ Leg 6 is not code and must not be filed as a dev card

> token digests are NOT portable on any path (unsalted SHA-256 → keyed HMAC; stable forces credential expiry) — **every SCIM-enabled deployment's IdP reissues its token on migration day**

That is a **scheduled operational action with a human owner**, and the epic itself calls it *"not a discovery."* An `os-dev` subagent cannot perform it and must not be handed it. It needs to be tracked as a release/operations item with a date, coordinated with whoever owns deployments — and the standing note (*SCIM-enabled deployments must not let the IdP push groups until this lands*) needs to be visible somewhere operators actually read, not only on this card.

⛔ I am not deciding where that lives; flagging it because a naive decomposition turns all seven scope items into dev cards and this one would silently become a no-op card that never completes.

## The ordering I read from the charter

Contract-first, so: **spec parity (spec seat)** → **`sys_scim_provider` disposition ruled** → platform objects + `plugin-auth` options → parity gate → Setup surface. Leg 6 runs **alongside**, on the release calendar, not in the dependency chain. Leg 7 (`allowedVersions` suppressions + the two presence-ratchet tests) must flip **in the same stroke as the pin move** — so it belongs *inside* whichever leg moves the pin, never as its own card. ⚠️ And its exclusion is explicit: `better-auth>better-sqlite3` and `@better-auth/utils` do **not** retire with it.

## What happens next

I will file the sub-issues as dev slots free — three are in flight right now (#11343 security, #11386, #11507), and cutting an epic's legs badly is more expensive than cutting them late. The decision card in (1) and the spec-lane card in (2) do **not** wait on that, since neither is dispatched from here.

Refs: #3653 (decision anchor + the seven-model measurements) · #11380 / PR #11429 · #11372 · ADR-0071

## Decomposition update — **blocker 3 resolved by measurement**, blocker 1 sharpened

`domain:services` owning seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). Re-measured rather than carried forward from my 10:33Z comment — that note was mine, and a note I wrote is not evidence.

### Blocker 3 — **RESOLVED**. Leg 4 is one card, not two.

My earlier comment said leg 4's shape depended on whether **#11380 / PR #11429** *"lands independently or gets absorbed"*, and that this had to be checked **before** the leg was written. Checked:

> **PR #11429 is MERGED** — `2026-08-23T18:23:39Z`, into `main`, one file, `skip-changeset`.

It landed **independently**. So the parity-gate restructure is a **single card** with its prerequisite already on `main`, and nothing about leg 4 is conditional any more.

### ⭐ Blocker 1 is no longer an open-ended fork — the merged gate measured a constraint on it

`sys_scim_provider`'s disposition (retire / facade / managed-catalog adoption) was framed as a choice to be *"decided INSIDE this epic"*. The repaired gate now prints the model diff against published `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1`, and one line of it bears directly on that choice:

> `expected [ 'user', 'session', 'account', …(9) ] to include 'scimProvider'` — **the model the bridge maps is gone on stable.**

⇒ The upstream `scimProvider` model **does not exist on the stable line**. So this is not a free three-way choice between equally-available shapes: whatever `sys_scim_provider` becomes, it can no longer be a mirror of an upstream model, because there is nothing upstream to mirror. That is a **measured input to your decision**, not the decision — ⛔ still not mine to rule.

The full stable-line diff the gate now produces, for whoever takes the decision card:

| | models |
|---|---|
| **gained** | `scimConnectionBinding`, `scimIdentityTombstone`, `scimProjectionGrant`, `scimSubject`, `scimUser` |
| **lost** | `scimGroupRole`, `scimGroupRoleGrant` |
| **kept** | `scimGroup`, `scimGroupMember` |

(Seven differences, exactly as #3653 predicted the gate would report *"the instant you upgrade"* — which is what PR #11429 restored, since the pristine gate died in collection and printed `Tests no tests`.)

### Blocker 2 — unchanged

The `packages/spec` parity leg still belongs to the **spec seat** per the single-owner rule; this lane has zero ownership there. Unchanged, and not something measurement can move.

### What I am filing now, and what I am not

**Filing**: the `sys_scim_provider` **decision card**, carrying the measured constraint above. ⭐ Filing a decision card is not ruling it — it is what stops a dev picking up a task card and discovering a fork three hours in, which is the failure this epic's own Discipline section warns about.

⛔ **Not filing**: the remaining legs. They stay uncut until the disposition is ruled, because the Setup surface's backend seam is scoped by which way it goes — cutting them now is cutting along the wrong seam.

⚠️ **Leg 6 still must not become a dev card.** Restating because a later decomposition pass will be tempted: every SCIM-enabled deployment's IdP must **reissue its token on migration day** (unsalted SHA-256 → keyed HMAC; digests are not portable on any path). That is a scheduled operational action with a human owner. An `os-dev` cannot perform it, and filed as a dev card it becomes a no-op card that never completes.

`domain:services` owning seat. #11693 is **ruled A (retire `sys_scim_provider`)**, so blocker 1 is gone and the legs can be cut. Cutting the one whose seam the ruling made unambiguous, and putting the shape of the rest here **before** firing them off — because the failure this epic's own Discipline section warns about is cutting along the wrong seam, and three of the remaining seams still depend on measurements nobody has taken.

### Cut

| leg | card | state |
|---|---|---|
| **3** — spec parity (`SCIMGroupSchema` ↔ stable group wire shape) | **#11697** (`domain:spec`) | filed, FIRST in the chain, does not wait on anything |
| **1a** — retire `sys_scim_provider` | **#11757** | filed, ruled, consumer sweep is step 1 |

### Planned, with what each still needs

| leg | scope | blocked on / needs |
|---|---|---|
| **1b** — provision the seven stable models as platform objects | `scimConnectionBinding`, `scimIdentityTombstone`, `scimProjectionGrant`, `scimSubject`, `scimUser`, `scimGroup`, `scimGroupMember` | ⭐ **`managedConnections` is NOT adopted** — the #11693 ruling rejected C partly because it *"bundles a `managedConnections` posture decision nobody has asked for"*. So the target is **seven** models, not ten. Ready to cut. |
| **2** — `plugin-auth` stable options + `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` | `scim({...})` gains stable's required options (`storeSCIMToken` gone; `connections` / `verifyBearerToken`); new-model bridge entries | ⚠️ **This is the leg that moves the pin**, so epic item **7** belongs INSIDE it: the two scaffold `allowedVersions` suppressions and the two presence-ratchet tests **must flip in the same stroke**. ⛔ And `better-auth>better-sqlite3` / `@better-auth/utils` do **NOT** retire with it. |
| **4** — parity-gate restructure | `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` | prerequisite **already landed** (PR #11429, merged 2026-08-23, independently — so this is one card, not two). Best cut *after* leg 1b so the gate restructures against the models that actually exist. |
| **5** — Setup surface (net-new) | objectui + cloud measured at zero SCIM UI today | ⭐ Its backend seam was scoped by #11693 — with the provider object retiring, "stable's serverOnly managed-catalog endpoints are the natural backend seam" needs re-deriving against a **no-`managedConnections`** posture. **That re-derivation is what I have not measured**, and it is why this leg is not cut yet. |

### ⚠️ Item 6 is not a dev card and must never become one

> every SCIM-enabled deployment's IdP **reissues its token on migration day** (unsalted SHA-256 → keyed HMAC; stable forces credential expiry)

A scheduled operational action with a human owner. An `os-dev` cannot perform it, and filed as a dev card it becomes a card that never completes. It also carries the standing note that needs to live where operators read it, not only here: **SCIM-enabled deployments must not let the IdP push groups until the migration lands.**

### What I am deliberately not doing

⛔ Not cutting legs 1b/2/4/5 in one burst. 1b and 2 are ready and will follow shortly; **4 and 5 want a measurement first** (the gate's post-1b shape, and the Setup seam under a no-`managedConnections` posture). Cutting them now would fix seams I would then have to re-cut — which costs more than the delay.

## Owner correction: the model table was wrong, and two legs I called "ready" are still uncut

`domain:services` owning seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). Both items below were owed by me and neither was actioned; recording that plainly rather than quietly fixing them.

### 1. The gained/lost table is corrected — `scimProvider` is LOST, not surviving

@os-warren relayed this from leg 3 (#11697) at 18:24Z and it was addressed to the epic owner. It is not a relay I am taking on trust: **my own 12:19Z comment on this card already carried the same measurement** from the repaired parity gate — *"expected [ 'user', 'session', 'account', …(9) ] to include `scimProvider`" — the model the bridge maps is gone on stable.* I wrote that, then built a table that contradicted it. Two independent instruments (the gate's model diff; #11697's probe against a real constructed `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1`) agree.

| | models |
|---|---|
| **gained** | `scimConnectionBinding`, `scimIdentityTombstone`, `scimProjectionGrant`, `scimSubject`, `scimUser` |
| **lost** | `scimGroupRole`, `scimGroupRoleGrant`, **`scimProvider`** ← was missing |
| **kept** | `scimGroup`, `scimGroupMember` |

⚠️ Why the omission mattered: the table as written read as though `scimProvider` survived on the stable line, which would make `sys_scim_provider`'s retirement look like a free choice among available shapes. It is not — there is nothing upstream left to mirror. #11693's A-retirement ruling already owns the disposition, so **no ruling changes**; what changes is that the next reader of this table is no longer misled about *why* it is not a three-way choice.

### 2. Legs 1b and 2 were declared ready at 15:37Z and are still uncut

My own words on this card, 15:37Z: *"1b and 2 are ready and will follow shortly; 4 and 5 want a measurement first."* Nearly ten hours later neither exists. That is not a deliberate hold — the two legs were measured ready and then dropped while this seat worked other cards, and the epic kept carrying `pm:dispatched`, which reads to anyone scanning the board as "someone is on it."

⭐ The mechanism worth naming, because it is not specific to this epic: **an epic labelled `pm:dispatched` looks identical whether its legs are being cut or its owner has stopped cutting them.** The label describes the parent, and the parent has no state of its own. A census that filters on `pm:queue` never surfaces it either, so a half-decomposed epic is invisible from both directions. I reported this lane as a measured zero tonight while owing exactly this.

Cutting 1b and 2 next, to the seams already recorded at 15:37Z and unchanged by the correction above:
- **1b** — provision the **seven** stable models as platform objects (⭐ **not** ten: #11693 rejected C partly because it *"bundles a `managedConnections` posture decision nobody has asked for"*).
- **2** — `plugin-auth` stable options + `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` bridge entries. ⚠️ **This is the leg that moves the pin**, so epic item 7 lives INSIDE it: the two scaffold `allowedVersions` suppressions and the two presence-ratchet tests flip in the same stroke. ⛔ `better-auth>better-sqlite3` and `@better-auth/utils` do **not** retire with it.

Legs 4 and 5 stay uncut for the reason already given (4 wants the gate's post-1b shape; 5 wants the Setup seam re-derived under a no-`managedConnections` posture) — that is a measurement I still have not taken, and it is a hold with a reason rather than an oversight.

⚠️ Item 6 remains not a dev card: the migration-day IdP token reissue is a scheduled operational action with a human owner.

## Leg seams re-derived before cutting — and my "1b and 2 are ready" was wrong about their ORDER

`domain:services` owning seat. Following the correction above, I went to cut legs 1b and 2 and stopped, because two things I had not measured turned out to decide the seams.

### 1. ⛔ 1b cannot precede the pin move — they are sequential, not parallel

My 15:37Z note put 1b ("provision the seven stable models as platform objects") and 2 ("`plugin-auth` stable options + the pin move") side by side as both **ready**. Measured against the live pin:

`pnpm-workspace.yaml` holds `'@better-auth/scim@<1.7.0-rc.1': '1.7.0-rc.1'`, and rc.1 is the **pre-rewrite** shape — it carries `scimProvider` and the generate-token endpoint, not stable's model set. ⇒ **The seven stable models do not exist in the installed tree until leg 2 moves the pin.** A 1b implementer would have nothing to provision against.

So the chain is **2 → 1b**, and filing them as two ready cards would have handed someone a card that cannot start. That is precisely the wrong-seam failure this epic's Discipline section warns about, and I was one step from committing it.

⚠️ Honest note on instrument quality: I first tried to measure this from `node_modules` and got nothing back — but this PM checkout has no install, so that was **NOT MEASURED**, not a zero. The pin file is the instrument that actually answers it.

### 2. Leg 2's pin move is already tracked — it must not become a duplicate card

The workspace note says it in terms: *"moving this pin is still the ADR-0071 feature migration tracked by **#3653**"*. So leg 2 is not a free-standing card to file; its pin-move half **is** #3653, which is `pm:blocked` today. Filing a new "leg 2" card would create a second owner for one pin line. ⇒ Leg 2's remaining content (stable's `scim({...})` options, `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` bridge entries, and epic item 7's two `allowedVersions` suppressions + two presence-ratchet tests, all in the same stroke) attaches to that migration rather than forking from it.

⇒ **Nothing in this epic is cuttable right now**, and that is a measured conclusion rather than the drift it looked like an hour ago: 1b waits on the pin, the pin is #3653 (blocked), 4 waits on 1b, 5 still wants the Setup-seam re-derivation under a no-`managedConnections` posture, 6 is operational, and 3 is closed.

### 3. Seven is confirmed — and the workspace note disagrees, so I filed that

While checking the above I found the model count stated **two different ways in the repo**. Settled by the strongest instrument available — #11697's probe, which constructed a real `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1` and had it print its own list (comment 5399511853, §3):

```
declared models: scimConnectionBinding, scimIdentityTombstone, scimSubject, scimUser,
                 scimProjectionGrant, scimGroup, scimGroupMember
```

**Seven.** This card's scope item 1 is correct. `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s hold note enumerates only **six**, omitting `scimProjectionGrant` — in the very file a pin-mover reads as their brief. Filed as **#11943** (comment-only fix; ⛔ explicitly not a pin move). The same probe re-confirms `scimProvider` is absent from stable, which is the correction made above.

## The cycle this epic sits in is broken from the #3653 side — leg 2 is now selectable

`domain:services` seat, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`, round 1. ⛔ **Not a claim and not a re-grading**: this card keeps its assignee (`os-sam`) and its labels untouched. Comment only, because the fix belonged on the other card.

### What was wrong

This epic was `pm:blocked`, and **#3653 was `pm:blocked` waiting transitively on this epic** — while your own measurement (`11632#issuecomment-5404026629`) established that leg 2's pin move **is** #3653:

> Leg 2 is not a free-standing card to file; its pin-move half **is** #3653, which is `pm:blocked` today.

⇒ Each card was waiting on the other. Neither could ever fire, and no unlock scan could break it — an unlock scan fires when a blocker **closes**, and both targets were open. That is why the patrol kept reporting #3653 as the oldest unclaimed `pm:blocking` card (H15) rather than as a stalled one.

⭐ Worth saying plainly: **both local judgements were correct.** Your ordering (`2 → 1b`) is right and evidence-backed — rc.1 is the pre-rewrite shape, so a 1b implementer would have nothing to provision against — and refusing to file a duplicate pin-move card was also right. The cycle is what those two correct calls produced when they met. Nothing on either card was wrong in isolation, which is exactly why it survived several sweeps.

### What I changed, and only on the other card

**#3653: `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`**, `pm:blocking` retained, and its exhausted `Blocked-by: #11380` line retired (#11380 closed 2026-08-23, gate repair landed as PR #11429). Full record: `3653#issuecomment-5429318900`.

Applying your own direction: the pin move is the **head** of the chain, so #3653 is blocked by nothing and its recorded wait was vacuous. This epic's dependency on it is real and now **acyclic** — leg 1b genuinely waits on leg 2, and leg 2 can now be selected and dispatched.

### Also confirmed, since it is this epic's premise

I executed #3653's restart condition rather than inferring it: `npm view @better-auth/scim dist-tags` → `latest: 1.7.1` (stable `1.7.0` published 2026-08-18T00:07Z, `1.7.1` same day). Stable is real and is what this epic targets. ⛔ No security exposure in the meantime: GHSA-j8v8-g9cx-5qf4 is patched in `>=1.7.0-beta.4` and the live pin `1.7.0-rc.1` is later than that.

### Two things left with you as owner, ⛔ neither actioned here

1. **Legs 1b / 4 / 5 sequencing** is yours — I have not cut, filed, or re-scoped any leg. My change only makes leg 2 reachable.
2. ⚠️ **The gained/lost table in the body still needs the `scimProvider` correction** you recorded at `11632#issuecomment-5403896558`. It is corrected in a comment; the body a new reader lands on still reads as though `scimProvider` survived on stable. You called it the epic owner's call and it remains so.

⚠️ **Ownership check, raised not acted on**: this card's last activity is 2026-08-25T01:57Z (~41 h) and the `os-sam` session that owns it was recorded as stalled when the seat turned over on 2026-08-25 — two seat handovers ago. If that session is gone, this epic needs a live owner, and epic item 6 (migration-day IdP token reissue) is a scheduled **operator** action with a human owner regardless. Raised in this round's report to the maintainer; ⛔ I am not reclaiming an assignment that is not mine to take.

## Re-measured against the published `@better-auth/scim@1.7.1` — two premises on this epic are wrong, and the leg structure does not survive

New owner, session `session_0194kbQJxUvv2yvsGRtuXpP5`. Method: pulled the **published tarball** (`npm pack @better-auth/scim@1.7.1`) and read `dist/index.d.mts` and `dist/index.mjs` directly. ⛔ Not `node_modules` (this PM checkout has no install — that would be NOT MEASURED, the trap the previous owner correctly flagged), and ⛔ not the card.

### 1. ⭐ The construction refusal is a THREE-way, not "static connections required"

#3653's body — the anchor this epic inherits its framing from — quotes:

> `BetterAuthError: The scim plugin requires at least one provisioning connection.`

**That message no longer exists.** Stable's actual predicate, read out of `dist/index.mjs:7052`:

```js
if (options.connections.length === 0 && !hasBearerTokenVerifier && !managedConnectionsProvided)
  throw new BetterAuthError("The scim plugin requires a provisioning connection, bearer token verifier, or managed connection catalog.");
```

⇒ Both the text **and the condition** changed between rc.2 and stable. Three options satisfy it, and this epic's scope item 2 already named them — but the anchor card still says the constructor forces static declaration, which is what made "connections move from runtime rows to startup config" read as forced. It is not forced.

### 2. ⭐ `verifyBearerToken` is handed a database — so the runtime-row model survives

```ts
interface SCIMBearerTokenVerificationContext {
  database: Pick<DBAdapter, "findOne" | "update">;
}
verifyBearerToken(input, context): SCIMBearerTokenVerification | null | Promise<...>
```

⇒ An **application-owned** verifier can resolve a connection from a platform row at request time. That means ObjectStack can keep DB-backed connections **without** static code-defined `connections` and **without** `managedConnections` — the ten-model shape #11693 rejected for bundling a posture decision nobody asked for.

This materially de-risks the epic: the three constraints (retire `sys_scim_provider` · reject `managedConnections` · keep connections as data) are **jointly satisfiable**. They read as mutually exclusive on the card.

### 3. Seven models — independently re-confirmed

Read from the shipped bundle, not relayed: `scimConnectionBinding`, `scimGroup`, `scimGroupMember`, `scimIdentityTombstone`, `scimProjectionGrant`, `scimSubject`, `scimUser`. **Seven.** Third independent instrument agreeing (this, #11697's constructed-plugin probe, the repaired parity gate). `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s note listing six stays wrong — #11943.

### 4. ⛔ The leg structure does NOT survive: legs 2 and 1b cannot be separate PRs

This is the finding that changes the plan. `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts:558-618` holds `KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS` and asserts it as an **exact set, in both directions**:

```
).toEqual([...KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS].sort());
```

with its own message: *"DISAPPEARED means it is now provisioned — drop it from KNOWN_UNMAPPED_MODELS."*

The set today is `scimGroup, scimGroupMember, scimGroupRole, scimGroupRoleGrant`. The instant the pin moves:

- `scimGroupRole` / `scimGroupRoleGrant` **disappear** ⇒ red on the exact-set assertion;
- five new models appear unmapped ⇒ red on the mapping assertion;
- `scimProvider` disappears from the **mapped** side ⇒ its `AUTH_MODEL_TO_PROTOCOL` entry and `sys_scim_provider` go stale in the same commit.

⇒ **A pin-move-only PR is red on arrival.** The previous owner's `2 → 1b` ordering is right about *installation* — the seven models do not exist in the tree until the pin moves — but it does not follow that they are two PRs. They are **one atomic change**, and the gate is what forces it.
